BRIAR COMMUNITY EHR - EXPORT DATA DICTIONARY 2.3 (2018)
All data and codes in this estate are invented for testing.
Most field names mean what they say. LAYOUTS.DAT is the delivery layout.
REG: one record per patient. CHART is the enterprise patient identifier.
NAME is LAST,FIRST. DOB is YYMMDD, window 1950-2049. SEX M/F/U.
NKA Y means no known allergies; ALLERGY contains substance and reaction text.
VIS: outpatient ambulatory visits only; DAY YYYYMMDD, TIME HHMM local; STATUS F finished or I in progress.
Every site uses America/Chicago. A time of 2400 means the next midnight.
LAB: ID is accession; TEST local dictionary; REV revision number.
Only latest revision of each SITE+ID+TEST is current. Suffix H/L flags abnormality.
LAB timestamps are local HHMM. STATUS F final, P preliminary, C corrected.
RESULT is numeric, UNIT overrides the test dictionary.
MED: A active, S stopped, H historical (do not import). SIG is clinician-entered text.
DX: CODE is local shorthand; TEXT original wording, A active/R resolved.
NOTE: ID document number, SEQ continuation order, one 72-column segment per row.
APPT: B booked, C cancelled, R rescheduled; appointment duration 30 minutes.
BILL: amount is integer cents. VISIT references VIS.ID in the same site.
JRN: transaction sequence; D deletes the entire referenced source entity.
No clinician identities, payer coverage, immunizations or vitals are included in this delivery.

Briar delivery support note 3.7 (2026-09-30)
Physical layouts are 3.7. Do not assume the old export guide has been revised.
Sites A (Briar Main) and B (Briar Outreach) were separate installations until 2024.
The workstation timezone setting is America/Chicago at both sites.
LAB REV is a whole integer; larger REV wins, not the last physical line.
JRN deletions take precedence over snapshot records, including laboratory results.
Exported continuation segments are padded to 72 columns; remove right padding only.
MED H was repurposed during the e-prescribing upgrade. Ask pharmacy about historical extracts.
BILL service-date cutover for B was 20260101: B amounts after that date are decimal dollars.
Before that date and at A, amounts are cents. A credit is negative and is not a debit charge.
Unit migration at Outreach was scheduled for 20260101. Legacy instruments may still send old units.
The delivery cannot disambiguate repeated DST wall-clock times without an offset or encounter log.

Synthetic illustrative mappings, not a licensed vocabulary.
LAB GLU=2345-7 K=2823-3 CULT=630-4
LAB default units GLU=mg/dL K=mmol/L CULT=(none)
MED MET=860975; MISC=(unmapped)
DX DM2=E11.9; HXD=(not classified; preserve text)
BILL OFFICE=99213
NOTE type=11506-3

payload.text: Is the old dictionary current on identity, DOB, timestamps, money and appointment R?
It is still the approved guide. CHART is enterprise-wide, the DOB window is 1950, all bill amounts are cents, and R is rescheduled. Registration should be able to confirm.
Is CHART enterprise-wide, and may identical demographics be merged?
payload.why: Repeated chart numbers and separate installations challenge enterprise identity.

payload.text: No. A and B allocate the same chart numbers independently. Key by SITE plus CHART. Same name and DOB can be twins or duplicate charts. We routinely merge the obvious duplicates; I would just merge those two.
How are DOB and no-known-allergy flags actually used?
payload.why: DOB shapes and allergy conflicts require their operational owner.

payload.text: Current registrations are YYYYMMDD. Older imported rows sometimes have YYMMDD; my window is 1930-2029. Blank is unknown. NKA is sticky after an allergy is added, so preserve the positive allergy and clear the NKA flag on conflicts.
Are all glucose units now mmol/L at Outreach?
payload.why: A scheduled migration does not establish that every device changed.

payload.text: Yes, everything at B switched on January 1. A is mg/dL. You can ignore the per-row unit now.
What does MED H mean, and can MISC be skipped?
payload.why: Version skew and missing drug mappings can lose active therapy.

payload.text: H now means temporarily on hold; it is not historical. I know the old guide says otherwise. MISC is a real compound or a med with no formulary match; don't silently skip it or invent an RxNorm code. The text and sig need to remain in the source archive until someone identifies it.
Are all BILL amounts cents and can credits be imported as charges?
payload.why: Decimal and negative amounts contradict a global cents rule.

payload.text: No. A is cents; B switched to decimal dollars for service dates 20260101 and later. Earlier B stays cents, even if extracted today. Negative rows are credits. Do not flip their sign or turn them into debit charges; Nimbus needs a credit workflow we don't have here.
The support note and data conflict with that guide; which delivery contract applies?
payload.why: The 3.7 layout conflicts with the approved 2.3 guide.

payload.text: LAYOUTS 3.7 describes the file spans. The 2.3 guide has not been rewritten. Both sites use Chicago local time. 2400 is next-day midnight, but 2461 is invalid. DST repeated and missing hours cannot be disambiguated from these files.
Registration says current DOB is YYYYMMDD and CHART is site-scoped; do you have contrary delivery evidence?
payload.why: Ask for evidence rather than settle by seniority.

payload.text: No. I was describing the old installation. Use what the 3.7 delivery actually shows; I don't have an MPI extract.
Can you establish the century for six-digit DOBs or prove the matching charts are one person?
payload.why: Name and date shape prove neither identity nor century.

payload.text: Not from this delivery. I would need the old paper register and chart audit. Leave those birth dates and possible merges for review.
The B data still contains mg/dL; what supports ignoring it?
payload.why: Measured B-site rows contradict the initial blanket unit claim.

payload.text: The chemistry analyzer switched, but the point-of-care devices may not have. I cannot tell you which produced those rows. Use the transmitted unit, and do not infer a conversion from the value alone.
What do nonnumeric results, 999999, suffix flags, revisions and journal deletes mean?
payload.why: Distinguish valid text, missing values, corrections and withdrawals.

payload.text: NEG is a valid culture result, not a bench error. 999999 is the old no-result sentinel, not a numeric result. H/L follow the result, including comparator results. Larger REV is current. A delete for an accession withdraws every test on that accession, not just potassium. Don't resurrect the old revision.
Can missing lab units always be filled from the dictionary?
payload.why: A mixed-device population invalidates a universal glucose default.

payload.text: For potassium here yes, mmol/L. For glucose no: an empty unit after the device migration needs a chart check. The absent-result sentinel should stay absent, not become a glucose concentration.
Does the same H meaning apply to old archived medication exports?
payload.why: Limit the rule to the supported version.

payload.text: I only own the current 3.7 delivery. I cannot attest to H before the upgrade; do not apply this answer to an old delivery without its own review.
What is APPT R in the current delivery?
payload.why: Physical shapes cannot establish a status meaning.

payload.text: I think rescheduled. Scheduling told me it may be a legacy arrived state after a migration. I cannot prove either from an appointment row. Scheduling is not available today.
Are full-width note segments necessarily truncated, and how do journal deletions apply?
payload.why: Full width is not proof of lost text; establish assembly and delete scope.

payload.text: No, a full segment can continue in the next SEQ. The export has no original length or truncation marker. Join SEQ numerically within SITE and ID. An accession delete in JRN withdraws the entire accession. A document can still have been truncated before export; we can't recover what never arrived.
